title: Schema Design Principles for conversations.schema.json
description: A living document of design principles, diagnostics, and manipulations for conversations.schema.json. Each principle has a machine-checkable diagnostic (a Python or jq snippet) and a human-readable rationale. This file is itself a JSON document and should be kept updated in parallel with the schema and its validation runs. Principles are organised into categories: Naming, Structure, Documentation, Empirical Grounding, Composition Patterns, API Correspondence, and Integrity Constraints.

principles.title: All definition names are UpperCamelCase
principles.rationale: Consistent UpperCamelCase for definition names cleanly distinguishes schema type names from data field names (which are snake_case or camelCase). This means a $ref is always visually distinct from a property key — e.g. "uuid": {"$ref": "#/definitions/UuidV4"} is unambiguous at a glance.

diagnostic.description: Find any definition name that is not UpperCamelCase.

principles.title: Every definition's title matches its key
principles.rationale: The title field is the human-readable name of the schema. It should match the definition key exactly so that tooling (e.g. VS Code tooltips) shows the correct name.

diagnostic.description: Find any definition whose title does not match its key.

principles.title: All property keys in data schemas are lowercase or snake_case
principles.rationale: Property keys mirror the actual JSON data fields, which follow snake_case. UpperCamelCase keys would indicate a wrongly-renamed property (a bug we encountered during the timestamp/flags/display_content renaming).

diagnostic.description: Find any object property key that starts with an uppercase letter.

principles.title: Every definition begins with title, description, type (in that order)
principles.rationale: Consistent field ordering makes schemas easier to scan. title and description come first as the human-readable contract; type follows as the primary structural constraint. The only exception is the root schema, which begins with $schema.

diagnostic.description: Find any definition where title and description are not the first two fields in that order.

principles.title: Definitions are ordered in breadth-first referential encounter order
principles.rationale: Reading the definitions top-to-bottom should follow the same order as reading the schema by following $refs. This makes the file navigable as a solitary wave — unfolding and refolding a single schema at a time. The ToolInput* variants (unreferenced via $ref, only mentioned in descriptions) appear at the end in original order.

diagnostic.description: Verify that definitions appear in BFS encounter order starting from Conversation.

principles.title: The definitions key is the last key in the root schema
principles.rationale: The root schema header ($schema, title, description, type, minItems, items) is read first; definitions are a reference section consulted on demand. Keeping definitions at the bottom mirrors this reading order.

diagnostic.description: Check that definitions is the last key in the root schema.
diagnostic.snippet:
import json
with open('conversations.schema.json') as f:
    schema = json.load(f)
keys = list(schema.keys())
if keys[-1] != 'definitions':
    print(f'definitions is not last: it is at position {keys.index("definitions")+1} of {len(keys)}')

principles.title: Every required field is listed in properties
principles.rationale: A required field not present in properties is a schema error — the validator will require a field it cannot validate.

diagnostic.description: Find any required field that is not in properties.

principles.title: No explicit additionalProperties: true
principles.rationale: additionalProperties: true is the default in draft-4. Explicit occurrences are redundant noise. The meaningful values are false (closed schema) and absent (open schema).

diagnostic.description: Find any explicit additionalProperties: true.

principles.title: Every definition is reachable from the root via $ref
principles.rationale: Unreachable definitions are dead code. The only legitimate exception is ToolInput* variants, which are referenced only in descriptions (not $refs) as documentation of known tool input shapes.

diagnostic.description: Find definitions not reachable from the root via $ref traversal.

principles.title: Every $ref target exists in definitions
principles.rationale: A $ref to a non-existent definition will cause validators to fail with a confusing error.

diagnostic.description: Find any $ref that does not resolve to a definition.

principles.title: Every definition has both title and description
principles.rationale: Titles and descriptions are the primary documentation mechanism. They surface as tooltips in VS Code when the schema is used as a documenter wrapper, making the schema self-documenting at the point of data inspection.

diagnostic.description: Find definitions missing title or description.

principles.title: All descriptions end with a full stop
principles.rationale: Consistent punctuation. Descriptions are prose sentences and should be punctuated as such.

diagnostic.description: Find descriptions that do not end with a full stop.

principles.title: Definitions with API counterparts have a See: link
principles.rationale: Where a schema corresponds to a public Anthropic API concept, the description should include a See: URL pointing to the relevant documentation page. This grounds the schema in the authoritative source.

diagnostic.description: Find definitions whose description mentions 'API' or 'Corresponds to' but contains no 'See:' link.
diagnostic.snippet:
import json
with open('conversations.schema.json') as f:
    schema = json.load(f)
for name, defn in schema['definitions'].items():
    d = defn.get('description', '')
    if ('API' in d or 'Corresponds to' in d) and 'See:' not in d:
        print(f'{name}: mentions API but has no See: link')

principles.title: Fields typed as null note this empirical observation in their description
principles.rationale: A field typed as null is a strong empirical claim based on observed exports only. The description should note this explicitly so future maintainers know to relax the constraint if non-null values are observed.

diagnostic.description: Find fields typed as null whose description does not mention 'null' or 'observed'.

principles.title: Enums that are likely open sets say so in their description
principles.rationale: Many enums are inferred from a small number of exports and are likely incomplete. The description should explicitly note this to prevent future maintainers from treating them as exhaustive.

diagnostic.description: Find enum fields whose description does not mention 'open set' or 'exhaustive'.

principles.title: Discriminator fields are annotated with description: "(discriminator)"
principles.rationale: Fields whose sole purpose is to discriminate between union branches should be clearly marked. This aids both human readers and automated tools.

diagnostic.description: Find enum fields with a single value that are not annotated as discriminators.

principles.title: The schema must validate against all known exports
principles.rationale: The schema is reverse-engineered from real data. Every known export is a ground-truth test case. A failing export is always a schema bug, not a data bug.

diagnostic.description: Validate all known exports using jsonschema.Draft4Validator.
diagnostic.snippet:
import json
from jsonschema import Draft4Validator
with open('conversations.schema.json') as f:
    schema = json.load(f)
for export_file in ['conversations.json']:
    with open(export_file) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    errors = list(Draft4Validator(schema).iter_errors(data))
    if errors:
        print(f'{export_file}: {len(errors)} error(s)')
        print(f'  First: {errors[0].message} at {list(errors[0].absolute_path)}')
    else:
        print(f'{export_file}: Valid')

principles.title: Every enum value is evidenced in at least one known export
principles.rationale: Unevidenced enum values may reflect guesswork or documentation-only values. They should be flagged and either evidenced or moved to a description note.

diagnostic.description: Collect all enum values from the schema and check each against values observed in the export.
diagnostic.snippet:
# Run after collecting observed_values dict from export data
import json
with open('conversations.schema.json') as f:
    schema = json.load(f)
# See empirical.oneOf_branches_evidenced for full collection pattern

principles.title: Every branch of every oneOf is evidenced in at least one known export
principles.rationale: An unevidenced oneOf branch may be speculative. It should be documented as such (e.g. 'Not observed in this export') rather than silently included.

diagnostic.description: Check that all oneOf branch types appear in the export data.

principles.title: Every tool_use_id in a ToolResultBlock matches a ToolUseBlock id in the same content array
principles.rationale: This cross-field constraint cannot be expressed in JSON Schema draft-4. It must be verified separately. Violation would indicate a malformed export.

diagnostic.description: Returns the number of content arrays passing the referential integrity check (should equal total number of content arrays containing tool_result blocks). Any error() call indicates a violation.
diagnostic.snippet: jq '[.[].chat_messages[].content | (map(select(.type=="tool_use")) | map(.id) | unique) as $ids | map(select(.type=="tool_result") | .tool_use_id) | map(. as $t | $ids | index($t) // error("unmatched tool_use_id: "+$t))] | length' conversations.json

principles.title: Discriminated unions follow the wrapper/base/subtype pattern
principles.rationale: A discriminated union is expressed as three layers: (1) a wrapper schema with title, description, type, allOf (base + Has*DiscriminatorProperty), and oneOf (subtypes); (2) a ...Base schema with additionalProperties: false and all shared fields; (3) n subtype schemas each with the discriminator field constrained to a single enum value. This pattern was developed iteratively and validated against draft-4 constraints. Key insight from proof-of-concept: allOf and oneOf sit at the wrapper level, not inside the subtypes, which avoids additionalProperties conflicts.

diagnostic.description: Find oneOf wrappers that are missing allOf with a Has*DiscriminatorProperty.

principles.title: Discriminator enum values across all branches of a oneOf are mutually disjoint
principles.rationale: A discriminated union requires that no value can match more than one branch. If discriminator enum values overlap across branches, oneOf will match multiple branches and validation will fail.

diagnostic.description: For each oneOf, collect discriminator enum values from all branches and check for overlap.

principles.title: All ...Base schemas have additionalProperties: false
principles.rationale: The ...Base schema is the definitive closed contract for all shared fields. additionalProperties: false ensures no unexpected fields pass validation, and that future Anthropic changes to the export format are caught immediately.

diagnostic.description: Find any ...Base definition missing additionalProperties: false.

principles.title: Union wrapper schemas have exactly five fields: title, description, type, allOf, oneOf
principles.rationale: The wrapper is a pure structural combinator. It should contain no additional constraints beyond those expressed by allOf and oneOf. Extra fields would conflate the wrapper with the base.

diagnostic.description: Find union wrapper schemas that do not have exactly the five expected fields.

principles.title: Repeated schemas are factored into definitions and referenced via $ref
principles.rationale: Inline duplication makes the schema harder to maintain and creates inconsistency risk. Any schema that appears more than once should be a named definition. This was applied to NullableString, NullableBoolean, Timestamp, Flags, DisplayContent, IntegrationName, IconName, etc.

diagnostic.description: Find identical inline schema objects that appear more than once (potential $ref candidates).

principles.title: The export format is the Claude API data model plus a persistence/UI envelope
principles.rationale: The core ContentBlock discriminated union (text, tool_use, tool_result) is shared verbatim with the API. Envelope fields (start_timestamp, stop_timestamp, display_content, integration_*, icon_name, approval_*, is_mcp_app, mcp_server_url) are claude.ai additions. Knowing this distinction helps when new fields appear in exports: they are likely either (a) new API fields or (b) new UI envelope fields, and should be documented accordingly.

principles.title: Export uses sender: human/assistant; API uses role: user/assistant
principles.rationale: The export renames 'user' to 'human' for the sender field. This is a known divergence from the API. Any schema update that changes the sender enum should be aware of this.

diagnostic.description: Verify observed sender values in the export.
diagnostic.snippet: jq '[.[].chat_messages[].sender] | unique' conversations.json

principles.title: Some tool names are claude.ai-internal with no public API documentation
principles.rationale: recent_chats, conversation_search, and recommend_claude_apps are claude.ai-internal tools. They appear in exports but have no public API documentation. New tool names should be investigated to determine whether they are public API tools or internal ones.

diagnostic.description: List all distinct tool names observed in the export.

principles.title: tool_use_id in ToolResultBlock references id of ToolUseBlock in same content array
principles.rationale: This is a cross-field referential integrity constraint that cannot be expressed in JSON Schema draft-4. It must be verified separately via jq or Python. Verified empirically: zero violations across all known exports.

diagnostic.description: Returns count of content arrays passing integrity check (checksum: 945 for the original export). Any error() indicates a violation.
diagnostic.snippet: jq '[.[].chat_messages[].content | (map(select(.type=="tool_use")) | map(.id) | unique) as $ids | map(select(.type=="tool_result") | .tool_use_id) | map(. as $t | $ids | index($t) // error("unmatched tool_use_id: "+$t))] | length' conversations.json

principles.title: Messages within a conversation are ordered by created_at
principles.rationale: Messages use UuidV7 (time-ordered) identifiers, and created_at timestamps should be monotonically non-decreasing within a conversation. Violations would indicate export anomalies.

diagnostic.description: Check that messages within each conversation are ordered by created_at.

principles.title: Every tool_use block has a corresponding tool_result block in the same content array
principles.rationale: The API requires tool results to be returned for every tool use. Unpaired tool use blocks may indicate truncated exports.

diagnostic.description: Check that every tool_use block has a matching tool_result block.

principles.title: UUIDs follow their declared format (v4 or v7) at each usage site
principles.rationale: Different fields use different UUID versions: v4 for conversations/accounts/citations, v7 for messages. Mixing them would indicate a data anomaly.

diagnostic.description: Check UUID version at each usage site.

principles.title: Workflow for incorporating a new export
principles.rationale: Each new export is both a test and a potential source of new schema knowledge. The workflow ensures the schema grows to cover new observations without losing existing constraints.

diagnostic.description: Steps to follow when a new export fails validation.
diagnostic.snippet:
1. Run Draft4Validator against the new export and note the first failing path and message.
2. Inspect the failing instance in the export to understand the new structure.
3. Determine whether this is: (a) a new field, (b) a new enum value, (c) a new oneOf branch, or (d) a nullable field that was previously always null.
4. Update the schema minimally to accommodate the new observation.
5. Add the new enum value/field to ToolName or the relevant definition.
6. Re-run validation against ALL known exports to confirm no regressions.
7. Update this principles document if the new observation motivates a new principle or diagnostic.
8. Note new tool names: check whether they are public API tools (add doc link) or claude.ai-internal (note as such).

principles.title: Use a redacted/compressed export for schema development
principles.rationale: The full export contains personal conversation content. A compressed version (with string values replaced by '[text]') is sufficient for schema development and safe to share. The compression workflow is: (1) replace non-empty string values with '[text]' via jq walk; (2) reduce arrays to first element; (3) validate the compressed version matches the full schema.

diagnostic.description: Compress an export by redacting string values.
diagnostic.snippet: jq 'walk(if type == "object" and has("text") and .text != "" and (.text | type) == "string" then .text = "[text]" else . end)' conversations.json > compressed.json

principles.title: Reapply BFS ordering after any structural edits
principles.rationale: Adding, removing, or reordering properties in a schema can change which $refs are encountered first, shifting the BFS order. The BFS reorder script should be run after any edit that adds new definitions or changes property order.

diagnostic.description: Reapply BFS ordering to definitions.
